target_customer: Data center operators and hyperscale builders in hot regions, starting with Texas
problem: Up to 40 percent of data center power goes to cooling, and chillers and cooling towers consume large amounts of power and water.
business_model: Hardware sales of modular dew-point cooling systems for new builds and retrofits

founders.name: Akshay Trikha
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Erik Meike
prior_employers: Apple (hardware development engineer, iPhone wireless power)

competitors.name: Munters
competitors.what: Data center chillers and cooling platforms, expanding to full cooling architecture
competitors.traction_then: established vendor growing its data center business

technical_complexity.rationale: Dew-point indirect evaporative cooling is known thermodynamics but making it modular, reliable and cheaper at hyperscale needs serious hardware engineering for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: A YC tier list review says dew-point cooling is not novel and cites earlier companies such as Coolerado; moat depends on execution and install base.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents already sell evaporative and chiller systems; no response to Madrone found.

market_need_then: AI data center buildout in 2025 to 2026 is straining power and water, and Texas has many new sites; an Uptime Institute April 2026 briefing argues dry cooling can match evaporative performance, so the claimed water advantage may be contested.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Concise and efficiency focused: Same grid permit. More compute. Made in California.

branding.community_and_virality: Site links a TBPN video and a Forbes article dated 2026-06-04 (not opened).

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive tagline and some media links, but minimal independent coverage found; a tree name shared with other firms.

outcome_analysis: Madrone is an active Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. The market pull from AI data center growth is strong, but the technology is not novel, incumbents are well resourced, and no installations or pilots were found in public sources, so proving the claimed 30 percent savings in the field is the key milestone.
notes: Unverified funding: Caplight and FundedIQ both show about 500k USD but disagree on the label (accelerator round dated 2026-03-01 versus pre-seed in 2026-06); both are aggregators, so no round is recorded. The Forbes article on the site was not found by search. Founder education for Trikha not found. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition.
